items.title: Follow up with client inquiries across channels
items.notes: Imported from an existing document.

sop.purpose: Govern how HighLife Studios follows up with anyone who contacts the studio across three channels (Website Form / Email, Call / Text, Instagram DMs), keeping messaging consistent and avoiding duplicate outreach to the same lead.
sop.trigger: A new inquiry is received via website form, email, missed call, text, or Instagram DM; every contact is automatically added to the CRM on first touch.
sop.inputs: CRM (contacts are auto-added on first touch); email list for ongoing email blasts; 20% off first-booking incentive shared across all channels.
sop.steps:
Website Form / Email: on new inquiry, auto-add contact to CRM
Reply to the inquiry by email the same day
If no response after 1–2 days, send follow-up #1 by email
If no response after another 1–2 days, make follow-up #2 call (form submissions only)
If no response after 3 days, send follow-up #3 by email offering 20% off first booking
If no response after 1 day, make follow-up #4 call repeating the 20% off offer
On completion of sequence, add contact to email list for ongoing email blasts
Send standing nurture touch every 90 days indefinitely by email or call
Call / Text: on new inquiry via missed call or text, auto-add contact to CRM
Make follow-up call the next day
If no response after 2 days, make another follow-up call
If no response after 2 more days, send follow-up text
If no response after 3 days, make follow-up call offering 20% off first booking
If no response after 3 more days, send follow-up text repeating the 20% off offer
Send standing nurture touch every 90 days indefinitely by text or call
Instagram DMs: reply to the DM the same day
Send follow-up DM the next day
If no response after 2 days, send another follow-up DM
If no response after 4 days, send follow-up DM offering 20% off first booking
Send standing nurture touch DM every 90 days indefinitely

items.title: Run Monthly HighLife Show (Concept to Post-Show Review)
items.notes: Imported from an existing document.

sop.purpose: Create small, repeatable, profitable, content-heavy monthly shows that a clear owner and the right partner can execute over and over, rather than building a giant event production every month.
sop.trigger: Monthly operating rhythm: while the current month's show is executed, next month's show is being recruited/announced/sold, and the show for month +2 (format, owner, partner, date) is being chosen — HighLife should not start from zero on the first day of every month.
sop.inputs: A repeatable format from the HighLife-owned format library (AUX Battle, Producer Battle, Hot Seat/Audition, Cypher/Freestyle, Creator/Podcast Show); one assigned Show Owner; one strong partner contributing at least one real asset (talent, audience, sponsors, venue access, credibility, or execution capacity); a written partner agreement covering responsibilities, money split, expenses, content ownership, and who collects payments; one-page economics with revenue target, maximum spend, break-even point, minimum participants, and minimum ticket sales; HighLife Management approval of the concept, budget, and key partner.
sop.steps:
Week 4 — LOCK IT: pick format, assign owner, lock date/venue, set pricing, confirm core partner, create ticket/registration link
Confirm partner responsibilities, money split, expenses, content ownership, and payment collection in writing before promotion begins
Confirm the one-page economics (revenue target, maximum spend, break-even, minimum participants, minimum ticket sales) before the flyer goes live
Week 3 — ANNOUNCE: launch flyer, start participant recruitment, confirm judge/host, begin sponsor/vendor outreach
Recruit participants directly (client database, previous performers/producers, Instagram DMs, engineer/staff referrals, partner networks, past attendees, local artist/creator communities) and track the funnel: Contacted -> Interested -> Registered -> Paid -> Confirmed -> Attended
Week 2 — BUILD MOMENTUM: post participants, judges, clips and stories; push direct DMs/texts; track registrations and ticket sales; if registrations or ticket sales are weak, fix the problem now
Week 1 — EXECUTE: final ticket push, confirm every participant, collect music/files, finalize one-page run of show, test production, assign show-day roles
Run pre-show content plan: main announcement, participant announcements, judge/host announcement, short promo video, stories and direct outreach, partner reposts
Show day — Setup: set room, audio, cameras, lights, check-in table, signage, and participant area (Production + Show Owner)
Show day — Doors/Check-In: check tickets, participants, vendors, and judges (Front Door / Show Owner)
Show day — Show: host follows the run of show; production captures the planned content (Host + Show Owner)
Show day — Winner/Final Moment: announce result, capture reactions, photos, and sponsor/partner moments (Show Owner + Production)
Show day — Close/Cleanup: clear room, confirm equipment, settle urgent partner needs, collect final notes (Team)
Capture during-show content: best performances/battle rounds, judge reactions, audience reactions, winner moment, quick participant interviews, behind-the-scenes moments
Within 24 hours: post winner/first recap, thank partners and participants, upload captured leads, record preliminary revenue/expenses
Within 72 hours: follow up with studio leads, release additional content, deliver promised participant assets, finalize payouts/expenses
Within 7 days: review the show against the five questions (money/business benefit, enjoyment, content, leads/relationships, improvements) and decide KEEP, FIX, or KILL
sop.qualityCheck: Non-negotiable rules: one show = one accountable owner; a repeatable format was used, not invented from scratch; break-even point was known before launch; the partner contributed real value; participant recruitment was direct, not just social posts; the show had a simple content plan; the show had a one-page run of show; the show received a KEEP / FIX / KILL review afterward. The show must not require a huge planning committee, complicated production plan, or six weeks of emergency work.
sop.sla: Four-week show cycle from concept to show day; post-show actions within 24 hours, 72 hours, and 7 days as specified; ongoing monthly rhythm (execute current month, sell next month, plan month +2).

Tours have a repeatable discovery and closing flow.
Recurring packages are being sold and retention is measured.
Monday leadership decisions are based on one scoreboard.
